### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **5** package(s): `@objectstack/core`, `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, `@objectstack/metadata`, `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/runtime`, touching **22** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-exact-qualifier.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**20** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 26f4e6d84af886706501e759b9385673615ee39e`.

⛔ **8** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-exact-qualifier.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **67** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 26f4e6d84af886706501e759b9385673615ee39e` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `9818f62d1bc06ac7f0eb1e07911d942c8f95ed97` — the merge of head `4403f2226729cf631bf1bd72363eadc80f8637f8` into base `26f4e6d84af886706501e759b9385673615ee39e`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 9818f62d1bc06ac7f0eb1e07911d942c8f95ed97 && git checkout 9818f62d1bc06ac7f0eb1e07911d942c8f95ed97
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 26f4e6d84af886706501e759b9385673615ee39e 4403f2226729cf631bf1bd72363eadc80f8637f8 && git checkout -B drift-repro 26f4e6d84af886706501e759b9385673615ee39e && git merge --no-ff 4403f2226729cf631bf1bd72363eadc80f8637f8

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 26f4e6d84af886706501e759b9385673615ee39e
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 26f4e6d84af886706501e759b9385673615ee39e` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `ddcaeda012c0000df1365e911ea12db825348131`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/core/src/package-scoped-resolution.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-meta-item-reads.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-meta-layered-reads.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-meta-item-reads.package-scoped-refusal.test.ts, packages/metadata/src/metadata-manager.ts, packages/metadata/src/package-slotted-store.ts, packages/metadata/src/metadata-manager-action-slots.test.ts, packages/qa/dogfood/test/action-slotted-store-artifact.dogfood.test.ts, packages/rest/src/meta-qualified-item-route.test.ts, packages/runtime/src/action-execution.ts, packages/runtime/src/action-package-addressing.test.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/meta-qualified-item-read.test.ts + read in the cited code, never reviewed: packages/objectql/src/registry.ts, packages/objectql/src/action-governance.ts, packages/objectql/src/action-package-addressing.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-exact-qualifier.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-meta-item-face.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-metadata-service-read.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-registry-hydration.ts, packages/rest/src/meta-item-history-routes.ts, ui/packages/app-shell/src/hooks/useNavActionDispatch.ts, docs/adr/0150 (D3, D5), content/docs/api/client-sdk.mdx, AGENTS.md (Post-Task item 3)

Inputs: card #32244's body and all its comments (through os-dev-report 6781208159), the PR #32361 body, its file list (13 files, +628 −32), the net diff against main (merge base 9bff554e), and the head's check-runs.

Check-runs on the head: 67, all completed. 56 success, 11 skipped, 0 failed. The dogfood shards are skipped on pull_request (ci.yml:2734), so the flipped dogfood pin has not run in CI here. The merge queue's build runs it. The dev ran that file alone 5/5, and the full battery on the pre-flip tree with only that pin red.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **Bare `GET /meta/action/NAME`: from 200 (first registered) to 409 `RESOURCE_CONFLICT` when two or more enabled packages hold the name on any object key. RIGHT.** `refuseActionHeldByPackages` (protocol-meta-item-reads.ts:130-148) runs before any layer is read (:255), as `registry.resolveItem` already does for every `readsByPackage` type. One package on two objects counts as one holder. `?package=` and the qualified path are untouched. Both transports are pinned.
2. **`/layers`: the same judge, at protocol-meta-layered-reads.ts:163. RIGHT but unpinned.** The only layered assertion (action-package-addressing.test.ts:472) builds a state where the registry counts one holder, so it passes through the store rethrow at :206. Deleting :163 leaves every test green (④ S2).
3. **`MetadataManager.get` / `getDiagnosed('action', NAME)` with no package: from written-last to the D3 refusal when the answering slots span two or more packages. RIGHT.** `refuseAcrossOwners` (package-slotted-store.ts:348-371) does exactly what card note 6773139204 orders. Package-less keys are skipped (:353); see ③.
4. **Both swallowing catches rethrow a recognised refusal (item-reads :720, layered :206). RIGHT.** It applies to every slotted type. For `api`, `agent` and `skill` the registry resolver already refuses first.
5. **Core export `packageScopedActionOwnersSentence` (package-scoped-resolution.ts:528-536). RIGHT.** It is public through `export *` and declared in the changeset. The new metadata-protocol helpers are module-level only.
6. **`/actions/:object/:name` via `routeOwnerOfRefusedRead` (action-execution.ts:5883, :5961-5994). RIGHT in the consistent state, and a real accept-set change.** Take A on `account` and B on `contact`. On main the bare read served whichever was registered first, so the other object's route ran with no declaration and no `requiredPermissions` or params gate. Now each route gets its own holder's declaration, which closes a fail-open. The changeset prose says so. The `Clause-②:` line does not (② S3).
7. **Undeclared door: REST `GET /meta/action/NAME/published`.** It makes the same bare read outside any inner catch (meta-item-history-routes.ts:1298; `getPublished` calls `this.get(type, name)`, metadata-manager.ts:2494-2495). The two-object pair therefore goes from 200 to 409 there too, and the changeset does not name it (④ S2).
8. **Dogfood pin flip. RIGHT.** The #31697 pin deferred this half to #32244. The flip keeps every other assertion and replaces "not refused, one of the two" with the refusal shape, the candidate order and a live HTTP 409 naming both objects.

### ② Semver level

`core`, `metadata`, `metadata-protocol` and `runtime` are each at `patch`, and each has a moved `src` file. `rest` and dogfood change tests only. `Metadata-protocol: none` is true: no authorable key, value or type moves. `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` is identical in the body and the changeset, with the BREAKING banner, the FROM → TO pair and one ADR-0087 marker. `Skills-docs: none` is true: no doc teaches a bare action read, and client-sdk.mdx:543-547 already promises the 409.

**S3 (should-fix):** the `Clause-②:` line names the `/meta` read and `MetadataManager.get` only. It should also name the `/actions` change (① 6) and the `/published` door (① 7).

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions` is empty. The deviations (action-execution.ts, the core helper, the dogfood pin) are each in a claim amendment (6779526112, 6779640498) or card note 6773139204.
- **Out-of-scope finding 1, confirmed, needs a card.** A package-less action on one object beside one package's action on another still picks written-last (package-slotted-store.ts:353), where D3 has the environment's item answer first for a caller with no package. The same card should take two more cases:
  - With two packages holding the name, an environment row binds to no one, and the 409 names no address for it.
  - With a disabled package registered first, the bare read answers no item although one enabled package holds the name (registry.ts:8531-8536, protocol-meta-item-face.ts:69). This is pre-existing on main.
- **Out-of-scope finding 2, confirmed, needs a card.** `restoreArtifactRegistryView` reads the service bare inside a silent outer catch (protocol-registry-hydration.ts:1421). After an overlay DELETE on such a name, the registry heal is skipped with no log line. `readCodeLayerForCarryForward` has the same bare read. Fix: pass the package.
- **Not flagged by the dev, needs a ui-lane card.** Console `useNavActionDispatch` calls `getItem('action', actionName)` with no package (useNavActionDispatch.ts:68). For such a name it now toasts "Could not load action" in both packages' apps. D5 has the Console pass the package it holds. First-party count is 0.
- Serial with #32329: the two collide only in package-slotted-store.ts's module doc, and the second to land resolves it.

### ④ Design judgment

The narrowing makes the spec's own refusal real (ADR-0150 D3 and D5: a bare address resolves while the name has one holder, and answers 409 otherwise, never a silent pick). It takes no declared capability away. Every holder stays reachable by `?package=`, the qualified path and `MetadataManager.get(type, name, holder)`, and `/actions` keeps each object's own holder.

Break attempts that held:
- one package plus an environment item;
- the same package on two objects;
- a disabled package, except the order dependency in ③;
- the catches now rethrowing: only the recognised refusal travels;
- recogniser false positives: the shape is `RESOURCE_CONFLICT` plus `refusal.status === 'refused'`, and the 501 carries another code;
- `/actions` with the object known and with it global;
- execution by object key: the declaration read at :5874 is the only bare action read in non-test code, and it is the one repaired;
- no protocol on the host: the fallback uses `loadDiagnosed`.

Findings:
- **S1 (should-fix). A candidate read that refuses becomes the route's answer (action-execution.ts:5981-5984).** When the store holds a package's item that the registry does not (the PR's own pinned state, test :455-473), `readAt(B)` throws `not-held-by-qualifier` naming A (protocol-exact-qualifier.ts:274). `/actions/account/approve` then answers a 409 about a package the caller never named, though A alone holds the route. It fails closed, and main ran it ungated, but ruling A wants the route's own key to answer. Fix: treat `not-held-by-qualifier` from a candidate as owning nothing, and pin it.
- **S2 (should-fix).** Pin `/layers` with a state where the registry counts both holders. Name `/published` in the changeset and pin it.
- **S3 (should-fix).** The `Clause-②:` line wording, as in ②.
- **S4 (should-fix).** The carriers of ③ are owed. The seat files them.
- **S5 (should-fix). "Naming every holder" fails with three holders.** `refuseAmbiguousObjectLessAction` runs first (:247-249). With two object-less package holders and a third package bound to an object, the 409 names only the two, and the third package's own `/actions` route is refused because recovery looks only at the refused candidates. Running the wider judge first, or merging the candidate sets, closes both.
- **N1 (nit).** "Each is a different action:" is also appended for two packages on one object.
- **N2 (nit).** `actionObjectOf` (:97-104) is a third spelling of the owner-key ladder, and `packageScopedRefusalOf` duplicates the runtime's `refusalOf`.
- **N3 (nit).** Stale prose still says an object-bound action reads through `getItem` unjudged: protocol-meta-item-reads.ts:246, protocol-exact-qualifier.ts:136-138 and registry.ts:8794.
- **N4 (nit).** The rethrow can name a disabled package when two others are live.
- **N5 (nit).** A registry without `packageScopedHoldersOf` skips the judge silently (:132).
- **N6 (nit).** Unpinned branches of `routeOwnerOfRefusedRead`: the object-less rung, two candidates on one rung, a non-package candidate, and a candidate read that throws.

No must-fix. S1 to S5 earn a fix round or follow-ups at the seat's choice; none makes the declared narrowing wrong.

**Epic red-line read — no PASS at `d055ebf7`** (#32244, a bare action read under two holders answers 409). One small required fix, R1 below.

**What holds**
- **The bare read refuses on every by-name surface.** `refuseActionHeldByPackages` refuses `GET /meta/action/NAME`, `/layers`, `/published` and `MetadataManager.get` (`refuseAcrossOwners`) when two or more enabled packages hold the name on any object key. Every holder is named with its object. A disabled holder is withheld, which is #32183's class.
- **The step-2 catch no longer swallows a refusal** (`rethrowPackageScopedRefusal`), which closes #32244's own defect.
- **The route's recovery mostly holds.** `/actions/:object/:name` reads each candidate at its exact address and takes only the object rung: the holder bound to the route's object, else the one object-less holder. Two holders on one rung keep the 409, a non-package candidate keeps the 409, and any other throw is an outage.
- **Changeset.** Clause-② yes (narrowing) is declared with FROM→TO.

**R1 (required): "a candidate read that refuses owns nothing" holds only for a not-held refusal**

`routeOwnerOfRefusedRead` treats every `PackageScopedNameRefusedError` from a candidate's exact read as "this candidate owns nothing" (`unread = true; continue`). If another candidate is on the rung, that one is served. This is right when the refusal is `not-held-by-qualifier`, the S1 state your pin covers, where B's address holds nothing and the refusal names A.

It is not right for a refusal that says the candidate's own address cannot be told. #32214 owes exactly such a refusal: a package-less row customizing two holders is refused at their exact addresses. Then candidate B's action is unknown, and it may be bound to the same object as A's. Serving A would pick between two possible owners of `object:name` (red line 2). This becomes reachable as soon as #32214 lands.

**Fix:** treat only `reason === 'not-held-by-qualifier'` as owning nothing. On any other refusal reason from a candidate's read, the bare read's refusal stands, whatever the other candidates answer. Pin it: B's read refuses `ambiguous-in-closure` (or any reason other than not-held) while A owns the route, and the route answers the 409.

**Note for the queue, not owed here:** #32365, #32366 and #32367 are carried, as recorded.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `02be22e672aceabeda7d3966358390a85d90cdaf`
Local-runs: none
Scope: .changeset/32244-ambiguous-bare-action-read.md, packages/runtime/src/action-execution.ts, packages/runtime/src/action-package-addressing.test.ts + read in the cited code, never reviewed: packages/core/src/package-scoped-resolution.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-exact-qualifier.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/actions.ts

Delta review of `d055ebf7..02be22e6`, on top of record 6784431291 (PASS at `d055ebf7`). The delta is one commit, 3 files, +36 −17. It answers item R1 of epic red-line read 6784464520 and claim amendment 6784476967. Everything outside it stands as judged in 6784431291.

Check-runs on the head: 67, all completed. 56 success, 11 skipped, 0 failed.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **The code does exactly what the order says** (action-execution.ts:5997-6002).
   - A `not-held-by-qualifier` refusal sets `unread` and continues.
   - Any other refusal reason returns the bare read's own refusal at once (:5999), whatever the other candidates answer.
   - A throw that is not a refusal is still an outage (:6003).
2. **The reason strings are real.**
   - All of them are members of `PackageScopedRefusalReason` (package-scoped-resolution.ts:338-358).
   - `not-held-by-qualifier` is what a package's exact address throws when it holds no item of the name and another holder does (protocol-exact-qualifier.ts:289).
   - `ambiguous-in-closure` is thrown by an exact read today (:334, :346), and it now keeps the 409.
   - The other two pinned reasons stand in for "any other reason".
3. **`refusalOf` reads `reason` from the right place** (:5616-5619). It returns the whole `PackageScopedRefusal`. A copy that lost its `reason` keeps the 409, which is the closed side. The 501 refusal is not `RESOURCE_CONFLICT`, so it stays an outage.
4. **The pin covers the order** (action-package-addressing.test.ts:591-598). The two not-held pins are respelled with a real `not-held-by-qualifier` refusal (:533, :578-589).
